get_favicon.description: Get a website's icon, the one browsers show in tabs and bookmarks, by its domain, a link to any page on it, or an email address at it: a link to the icon at the size you pick, an tag, its real size and whether the site has an icon of its own. Save it as a file to attach if you need to. No API key required.
get_favicon.name: get_favicon

parameters.description: The website whose icon you want: its domain, such as 'github.com', a link to any page on it, or an email address at it, whose domain is used.
parameters.name: website

parameters.description: Optional. The icon's width and height in pixels: one of the sizes Google serves. 64 by default. Google never enlarges an icon, so a site whose own is smaller comes back at its own size.
parameters.name: size

parameters.description: Off by default, because the link is all an email, a chat message or a web page needs. Turn it on when a later step needs the file itself: attaching it to an email, uploading it to storage, or posting it as a file.
parameters.display_name: Also save the icon as a file
parameters.name: save_as_file

content_type.description: The saved file's type, e.g. image/png, or '' when not saved.

document_ref.description: The saved file's document reference, or '' when not saved.

documents.description: The saved icon as a document, ready to attach to a later step. Empty when it was not saved.

filename.description: The file's name, built from the domain and the size, e.g. 'favicon-github.com-64.png'.

url.description: A URL that serves the stored file.

domain.description: The site's domain name as Google was asked for it, e.g. 'www.bbc.co.uk': a link or an email address comes down to its domain, in lower case, and a name in another script to its xn-- form.

file_size_bytes.description: The saved file's size in bytes, or 0 when not saved.

file_url.description: A URL that serves the saved file, or '' when not saved.

has_icon.description: True when Google has the site's own icon. False when it has none for the site, or the site does not exist, and sent its default icon, a small blue globe, which the link then shows.

height.description: The icon's real height in pixels.

image_tag.description: The same link as an HTML tag, with alt text, for a step that writes an email or a page. It shows the icon at the size asked for, so icons line up in a list whatever size each site's own is.

mimetype.description: The icon's file type as Google sent it: 'image/png' for most sites, 'image/jpeg' for a few.

saved_as_file.description: True when the icon was also saved as a file (Also save the icon as a file). The file fields below are empty otherwise.

size.description: The size asked for, in pixels, e.g. 64.

url.description: A link to the icon at that size on Google's servers, e.g. 'https://www.google.com/s2/favicons?domain=github.com&sz=64'. It can go straight into an email, a chat message or a web page.

website.description: The website as it was given, e.g. 'https://www.bbc.co.uk/news' or 'support@stripe.com'.

width.description: The icon's real width in pixels. Smaller than the size asked for when the site has no bigger icon, as Google never enlarges one: 16 for the default globe.

get_favicons.description: Get the icons of up to 50 websites at once, in the order given: for each, a link and an tag at the size you pick and whether the site has an icon of its own, with counts of those that do and do not. An entry that is not a website is reported rather than stopping the step. No API key required.
get_favicons.name: get_favicons

parameters.description: Up to 50 websites: domains, links or email addresses, separated by commas or on lines of their own, or a list from an earlier step. There is one result for each, in the order given, so the results line up with the list they came from.
parameters.name: websites

parameters.description: Optional. The icon's width and height in pixels: one of the sizes Google serves. 64 by default. Google never enlarges an icon, so a site whose own is smaller comes back at its own size.
parameters.name: size

get_favicons.result_str_template: Got favicons for {google_favicons_get_favicons,count} websites, {google_favicons_get_favicons,with_icon} with an icon of their own.

icons.description: One result for each website, in the order given.

domain.description: The site's domain name as Google was asked for it, e.g. 'www.bbc.co.uk': a link or an email address comes down to its domain, in lower case, and a name in another script to its xn-- form.

error.description: Why this entry could not be looked up, e.g. that it is not a website, or '' when it was. Its link, tag and domain are then '', its size in pixels 0 and has_icon false.

has_icon.description: True when Google has the site's own icon. False when it has none for the site, or the site does not exist, and sent its default icon, a small blue globe, which the link then shows.

height.description: The icon's real height in pixels.

image_tag.description: The same link as an HTML tag, with alt text, for a step that writes an email or a page. It shows the icon at the size asked for, so icons line up in a list whatever size each site's own is.

mimetype.description: The icon's file type as Google sent it: 'image/png' for most sites, 'image/jpeg' for a few.

size.description: The size asked for, in pixels, e.g. 64.

url.description: A link to the icon at that size on Google's servers, e.g. 'https://www.google.com/s2/favicons?domain=github.com&sz=64'. It can go straight into an email, a chat message or a web page.

website.description: The website as it was given, e.g. 'https://www.bbc.co.uk/news' or 'support@stripe.com'.

width.description: The icon's real width in pixels. Smaller than the size asked for when the site has no bigger icon, as Google never enlarges one: 16 for the default globe.

not_websites.description: How many entries could not be looked up: blank, or not a website. Their error says why.

with_icon.description: How many of them have an icon of their own.

without_icon.description: How many are websites Google has no icon for, shown with its default globe.

description: Get the icon of almost any website, the one browsers show in tabs and bookmarks (its favicon), from Google's public favicon service. Give a domain, a link or an email address and get a link to the icon at a size from 12 to 256 pixels, ready for an email, a chat message or a web page, whether the site has an icon of its own, and the icon as a file to attach. Look up to 50 websites at once. Google does not document the service or promise to keep it running. No account or API key required.
